title: 8 Peak Bead Tracking — Aurora EVO (5L)
text:
Secondary QC for the Cytek Aurora EVO (5L): RCP-30-5A 8-peak rainbow beads are acquired each run and tracked over time to catch instrument drift. The heavy work — reading the raw FCS, gating the beads, clustering the 8 populations and measuring each population in all 64 detectors — is done once per run by Process8Peak.R, which appends the results to peak_metrics.csv. This page only reads that archive, so it renders quickly and adds no load to the site build. (For per-run gating/clustering diagnostics, render 8peak_tracking_spectral/EVO_8 Peak Tracking.qmd on demand.)
Code
library(ggcyto)   # scale_*_flowjo_biexp axis; pulls in flowCore, which masks dplyr verbs
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)    # load LAST so dplyr's filter()/select() win the namespace masking

# Display-only: read the archive produced by Process8Peak.R. No FCS, no flowClust.
results_file <- if (file.exists("8peak_tracking_spectral/peak_metrics.csv")) {
  "8peak_tracking_spectral/peak_metrics.csv"
} else "peak_metrics.csv"
combined <- read_csv(results_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
combined$date <- as.Date(combined$date)

# Display constants — must match Process8Peak.R.
n_peaks          <- 8
biex_max         <- 4194304
biex_pos         <- 5.62
biex_neg         <- 0
biex_width_basis <- -250

# Detector acquisition order (UV -> V -> B -> YG -> R), derived from the archive
# so this page needs no FCS to know the channel layout.
laser_levels <- c("UV", "V", "B", "YG", "R")
det_order <- combined |>
  distinct(detector) |>
  mutate(laser = sub("[0-9]+-A$", "", detector),
         num   = as.integer(sub("-A$", "", sub("^(UV|V|B|YG|R)", "", detector)))) |>
  arrange(match(laser, laser_levels), num)
detector_channels <- det_order$detector
combined$detector <- factor(combined$detector, levels = detector_channels)

title: Measurement Types
text:
Gain (similar to voltage on certain cytometers) is an unit which detected signal is amplified by for each detector. An instrument applies different gains to each detector, allowing for use of dim and bright fluorophores. During the Daily QC, these gains normally get minor adjustments to keep the QC beads’ signal constant, allowing for comparison of .fcs files acquired on different days. As the individual lasers in the cytometer are used, they slowly wear down and more gain is applied to remain at that setpoint. This contributes to the slowly increasing view typical of the gain plots:





Generally, when a laser is begining to rapidly wear out, we see steeper increases in the Gain plots. When the field service engineer replaces the laser, the gain values are reset according to the new laser. In this example, you can see that pattern for the violet laser of the instrument was replaced twice (red lines indicating field service engineer visit):





For the Cytek instruments, a Daily QC fail is triggered when the Gain is >100% of the original baseline Gain value. When this happens, a red flag is added to that timepoint. We have observed that .fcs files acquired on gain spike days (as seen below) may still have altered unmixing even if they have not exceeded the >100% threshold, so it’s worth keeping an eye on.








The robust coefficient of variation (rCV) is a measure of the resolution between the positive and negative population for each detector. When the value is high, dim staining populations may be harder to distinguish from the negative population. For spectral instruments where entire spectrum is used to identify a fluorophore, increased rCV on the detector where a fluorophore has its main peak has impacted unmixing for users with larger panels (>20 fluorophores). The RCV plots will typically resemble the following:





For Cytek instruments, a Daily QC fail is only triggered when %rCV exceeds either 8% for SSC, or 6% for FSC and the following detectors: UV3, V3, B3, YG3, R3. When this happens, the instrument will appear as failed on the home page:





When we navigate to the History tab and find that date, we can see that the rCV for UV3 failed, which was what triggered the QC fail:





But what happens if the RCV fails on any of the other detectors (UV1-> UV2, UV4 -> UV16,etc.)? Since they are not the indicator detectors, they won’t trigger a Cytek QC fail. However, since we have observed unmixing issues when the RCVs of these other detectors are exceeded, we don’t want to ignore them. Consequently, when a non-indicator RCV fails, we show it as failed under the Daily View:





And label the instrument as caution for that given day:





How to interpret these Caution notices depends on what we see in the Levey-Jennings plots. For a few detectors (especially UV1/UV2), they exceed the 6% cutoff but are stable over time. Consequently, the impact of the increased RCV is relatively minimal.





By contrast, is the RCV went from consistently stable, to spiking, the impact on your unmixing is likely to be significantly greater.

title: 8 Peak Bead Tracking — Aurora EVO (5L)
text:
Configuration
All tunable parameters live here in one place: which channels count as detectors, the gating tightness, the biexponential display settings, the clustering anchors, and where results are saved. Adjusting the pipeline should only ever require editing this block.


Code
# A "detector" here is a fluorescence channel: laser-prefixed Area parameters
# (e.g. UV1-A, V3-A, B5-A, YG2-A, R7-A). Scatter and Time are excluded.
detector_pattern <- "^(UV|V|B|YG|R)[0-9]+-A$"

# Scatter channels used for gating the bead population.
scatter_x <- "FSC-A"
scatter_y <- "SSC-A"

# Bead gate tuning.
#   gate_distance -> Mahalanobis radius of the ellipse; larger keeps more.
# The ellipse centre/shape come from a high-breakdown (minimum-volume) robust
# fit that locks onto the dense bead core and ignores the low-scatter debris
# in the bottom-left corner. Retention plateaus around the core (~60-62%), so
# the exact distance is not critical.
gate_distance <- 4

# Histogram display: FlowJo-style biexponential ("Biex") axis. These match the
# SpectroFlo/FlowJo defaults for this instrument so the peaks line up with the
# acquisition software. maxValue is the Aurora's 2^22 data ceiling.
biex_max          <- 4194304
biex_pos          <- 5.62   # positive decades
biex_neg          <- 0      # extra negative decades
biex_width_basis  <- -250   # width basis (controls the linear region near 0)

# Singlet gate: a second ellipse on FSC-A x FSC-H removes doublets/aggregates
# so the peaks are tighter before clustering.
singlet_x        <- "FSC-A"
singlet_y        <- "FSC-H"
singlet_distance <- 4

# Peak clustering. The 8 RCP-30-5A populations are assigned ONCE per run by a
# multivariate model-based clustering, then read out in every detector. This is
# far more robust than per-detector peak detection, because weak detectors
# cannot resolve the dim peaks on their own but the strong "anchor" detectors
# can, and a bead's population is fixed across all detectors.
n_peaks         <- 8        # known number of bead populations (fixed K)
cluster_cofactor <- 150     # asinh cofactor for the clustering transform
# Anchor detectors used for clustering: a stable set with wide dynamic range
# (broadly excited, well-separated peaks). Chosen from the strongest resolving
# channels; clustering only needs a good subset, not all 64.
anchor_detectors <- c("UV9-A", "B4-A", "B7-A", "B8-A", "B9-A",
                      "V8-A", "R2-A", "YG3-A")

# A peak is "resolved" in a detector if its gap to the nearer neighbouring peak
# (on the asinh scale) exceeds this multiple of its own robust width.
resolution_k <- 2

# Detectors used only to visualise the cluster assignment (not the clustering
# itself). The 1D check uses the first anchor; the 2D check uses a pair that
# both resolve all 8 peaks, where the populations show as 8 separated blobs.
diag_detector_1d <- anchor_detectors[1]
diag_detectors_2d <- c("V1-A", "YG1-A")

# Accumulated per-run metrics are persisted here so the year builds up.
results_file <- if (dir.exists("8peak_tracking_spectral")) "8peak_tracking_spectral/peak_metrics.csv" else "peak_metrics.csv"

title: 8 Peak Bead Tracking — Aurora EVO (5L)
text:
Read FCS file(s)
Loads every .fcs in the data folder (filenames are YYYYMMDD.fcs, so the acquisition date is read straight from the name) and lists the event count per run. New runs are picked up automatically — just drop the file in the folder. The table below confirms each file was read and dated correctly.


Code
# Filename convention: YYYYMMDD.fcs -> acquisition date. Reading a folder
# returns every file, so adding future runs needs no code change.
read_runs <- function(dir) {
  files <- list.files(dir, pattern = "\\.fcs$", full.names = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE)
  if (length(files) == 0) stop("No FCS files found in: ", dir)
  setNames(lapply(files, read.FCS, transformation = FALSE), basename(files))
}

parse_run_date <- function(fname) {
  m <- regmatches(fname, regexpr("[0-9]{8}", fname))
  if (length(m) == 1) as.Date(m, format = "%Y%m%d") else as.Date(NA)
}

runs <- read_runs(data_dir)

detector_channels <- grep(detector_pattern, colnames(runs[[1]]), value = TRUE)

tibble(
  file   = names(runs),
  date   = as.character(vapply(names(runs), function(f) as.character(parse_run_date(f)), character(1))),
  events = vapply(runs, n_events, integer(1))
)

title: 8 Peak Bead Tracking — Aurora EVO (5L)
text:
Forward / side scatter gating
Isolates the beads from debris and aggregates before any intensity is measured. A robust ellipse on FSC-A × SSC-A locks onto the dense bead cluster (rejecting the low-scatter debris in the bottom-left corner), then a second ellipse on FSC-A × FSC-H removes doublets. The table reports how many events survive each step — typically ~60% beads, of which ~97% are singlets.


Code
# Automated, data-driven bead gate. MASS::cov.rob fits a minimum-volume
# ellipsoid (high-breakdown, ~50% of points) to FSC-A x SSC-A, which locks
# onto the dense bead cluster and rejects the low-scatter debris. The fit is
# expressed as a flowCore ellipsoidGate, so it adapts to small run-to-run
# shifts in scatter position without a hand-drawn polygon and works unchanged
# across the year's runs.
make_bead_gate <- function(ff) {
  m  <- exprs(ff)[, c(scatter_x, scatter_y), drop = FALSE]
  rc <- MASS::cov.rob(m)
  ellipsoidGate(filterId = "beads", .gate = rc$cov,
                mean = rc$center, distance = gate_distance)
}

# Singlet gate: same robust-ellipse approach on FSC-A x FSC-H, applied after
# the bead gate to drop doublets and aggregates before clustering.
make_singlet_gate <- function(ff) {
  m  <- exprs(ff)[, c(singlet_x, singlet_y), drop = FALSE]
  rc <- MASS::cov.rob(m)
  ellipsoidGate(filterId = "singlets", .gate = rc$cov,
                mean = rc$center, distance = singlet_distance)
}

apply_bead_gate <- function(ff) {
  Subset(ff, flowCore::filter(ff, make_bead_gate(ff)))
}
apply_singlet_gate <- function(ff) {
  Subset(ff, flowCore::filter(ff, make_singlet_gate(ff)))
}

beads <- lapply(runs, apply_bead_gate)
gated <- lapply(beads, apply_singlet_gate)   # final: singlet beads

local({
  input    <- vapply(runs,  n_events, integer(1))
  bead_n   <- vapply(beads, n_events, integer(1))
  singlet  <- vapply(gated, n_events, integer(1))
  tibble(
    file        = names(runs),
    input       = input,
    beads       = bead_n,
    singlets    = singlet,
    pct_beads   = round(100 * bead_n / input, 1),
    pct_singlet = round(100 * singlet / bead_n, 1)
  )
})


# A tibble: 3 x 6
  file         input beads singlets pct_beads pct_singlet
  <chr>        <int> <int>    <int>     <dbl>       <dbl>
1 20260520.fcs  8214  5055     4940      61.5        97.7
2 20260527.fcs  5595  4953     4885      88.5        98.6
3 20260529.fcs  5788  4968     4886      85.8        98.3



Gate visualisation
A visual confirmation that the bead gate landed on the right population: the scatter cloud is shown with retained (bead) events in red and excluded events in grey. The red cluster should be the tight, dense blob — not the debris.


Code
# Show the scatter cloud with retained (bead) events highlighted, per file.
gate_df <- function(name) {
  raw <- exprs(runs[[name]])[, c(scatter_x, scatter_y), drop = FALSE]
  res <- flowCore::filter(runs[[name]], make_bead_gate(runs[[name]]))
  data.frame(
    file = name,
    x    = raw[, scatter_x],
    y    = raw[, scatter_y],
    bead = res@subSet
  )
}

scatter_plot_df <- bind_rows(lapply(names(runs), gate_df))

ggplot(scatter_plot_df, aes(x = x, y = y, colour = bead)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.2, alpha = 0.3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "grey70", "TRUE" = "firebrick"),
                      labels = c("excluded", "bead"), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(scale_cut = scales::cut_short_scale())) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(scale_cut = scales::cut_short_scale())) +
  facet_wrap(~ file) +
  labs(x = scatter_x, y = scatter_y, title = "Bead population gate") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 2, alpha = 1))) +
  theme_bw()

title: 8 Peak Bead Tracking — Aurora EVO (5L)
text:
Per-detector histograms
The intensity distribution of the gated beads in every fluorescence detector, on a FlowJo-style biexponential axis. This is the raw picture of how well each detector resolves the 8 peaks: strong detectors show a clean 8-peak staircase, weak ones show fewer. The dashed red line marks the detector ceiling (4,194,304) — peaks pressed against it are saturated / out of range.


Code
# Melt the gated bead events to long form: one row per (file, detector, event).
# Raw intensities are kept; the display is handled by the plot's biexponential
# axis, which bins uniformly in biex space so the 8 peaks resolve.
to_long <- function(ff, name) {
  as.data.frame(exprs(ff)[, detector_channels, drop = FALSE]) |>
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "detector", values_to = "value") |>
    mutate(file = name)
}

hist_long <- bind_rows(base::Map(to_long, gated, names(gated)))

# Preserve acquisition order of detectors (UV -> V -> B -> YG -> R).
hist_long$detector <- factor(hist_long$detector, levels = detector_channels)




Code
ggplot(hist_long, aes(x = value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 256, fill = "grey50", colour = NA) +
  # Detector ceiling: events at this value are off-scale (out of range).
  geom_vline(xintercept = biex_max, colour = "firebrick",
             linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.4) +
  scale_x_flowjo_biexp(maxValue = biex_max, pos = biex_pos,
                       neg = biex_neg, widthBasis = biex_width_basis) +
  facet_wrap(~ detector, scales = "free_y", ncol = 4) +
  labs(x = "Intensity (biexponential scale)", y = "Count",
       title = "8-peak bead intensity per detector",
       caption = sprintf("Dashed red line = detector upper limit (%s); events at this value are out of range.",
                         format(biex_max, big.mark = ","))) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 9) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 8),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 6))

title: 8 Peak Bead Tracking — Aurora EVO (5L)
text:
Peak clustering
Assigns every bead to one of the 8 populations. Rather than detect peaks separately in each detector (unreliable where peaks merge), the 8 populations are identified once per run by multivariate clustering across the strong anchor detectors, then read out everywhere. Because a bead’s population is fixed across all detectors, even a weak detector that can’t resolve the dim peaks still gets a defined value for all 8. The table shows cluster sizes, which should be roughly even (the beads are mixed in equal proportions).


Code
# Assign each bead event to one of the 8 populations using flowClust (fixed
# K = 8) on the asinh-transformed anchor detectors. Clustering is multivariate:
# because the bead levels scale proportionally across dyes, the 8 populations
# are well-separated blobs in anchor space even where a single channel cannot
# resolve them. Labels are ordered 1..8 by ascending overall brightness so they
# are consistent across detectors and across runs.
assign_peaks <- function(ff) {
  te  <- asinh(exprs(ff)[, anchor_detectors, drop = FALSE] / cluster_cofactor)
  fit <- flowClust(flowFrame(te), varNames = anchor_detectors,
                   K = n_peaks, B = 500, trans = 0)
  lab <- flowClust::Map(fit, rm.outliers = FALSE)   # force-assign every bead
  brightness <- tapply(rowMeans(te), lab, median)
  rank_map   <- setNames(rank(brightness), names(brightness))
  as.integer(rank_map[as.character(lab)])
}

set.seed(1)
peak_labels <- lapply(gated, assign_peaks)

# Sanity check: RCP-30-5A mixes the 8 populations in ~equal proportions, so the
# cluster sizes should be roughly even.
local({
  tab <- sapply(peak_labels, function(p) table(factor(p, levels = 1:n_peaks)))
  out <- as.data.frame(t(tab))
  out <- cbind(file = names(peak_labels), out)
  out
})


                     file   1   2   3   4   5   6   7   8
20260520.fcs 20260520.fcs 609 647 605 609 647 625 590 608
20260527.fcs 20260527.fcs 620 585 580 595 606 600 631 668
20260529.fcs 20260529.fcs 591 600 601 589 656 602 615 632



Cluster diagnostic
Confirms the clustering worked before any metrics are trusted. The 1D view colours an anchor detector’s histogram by assigned population — it should be a clean, ordered staircase. The 2D view plots two detectors that both resolve all 8 peaks, where the populations appear as 8 separated, single-coloured blobs along the diagonal; this is the clearest check, since the dim-peak overlap of the 1D view disappears. Interleaved colours or scrambled order would signal a misassignment.


Code
# Validate the assignment: on an anchor detector the 8 labelled populations
# should form a clean, monotonically ordered staircase of peaks.
diag_df <- bind_rows(base::Map(function(ff, lab, name) {
  data.frame(file = name, value = exprs(ff)[, diag_detector_1d],
             peak = factor(lab, levels = 1:n_peaks))
}, gated, peak_labels, names(gated)))

ggplot(diag_df, aes(x = value, fill = peak)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 256, position = "identity", alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_x_flowjo_biexp(maxValue = biex_max, pos = biex_pos,
                       neg = biex_neg, widthBasis = biex_width_basis) +
  facet_wrap(~ file, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = sprintf("%s (biexponential scale)", diag_detector_1d), y = "Count",
       fill = "Peak", title = "Cluster assignment check (1D, anchor detector)") +
  theme_bw()











Code
# Clearer view: plotting two detectors that both resolve all 8 peaks shows the
# populations as 8 well-separated blobs along the diagonal (bead levels scale
# proportionally across dyes). Correct assignment = 8 tight, ordered, single-
# coloured clusters with no interleaving.
diag2d_df <- bind_rows(base::Map(function(ff, lab, name) {
  data.frame(file = name,
             x    = exprs(ff)[, diag_detectors_2d[1]],
             y    = exprs(ff)[, diag_detectors_2d[2]],
             peak = factor(lab, levels = 1:n_peaks))
}, gated, peak_labels, names(gated)))

ggplot(diag2d_df, aes(x = x, y = y, colour = peak)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.5, alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_x_flowjo_biexp(maxValue = biex_max, pos = biex_pos,
                       neg = biex_neg, widthBasis = biex_width_basis) +
  scale_y_flowjo_biexp(maxValue = biex_max, pos = biex_pos,
                       neg = biex_neg, widthBasis = biex_width_basis) +
  facet_wrap(~ file) +
  labs(x = sprintf("%s (biexponential scale)", diag_detectors_2d[1]),
       y = sprintf("%s (biexponential scale)", diag_detectors_2d[2]),
       colour = "Peak", title = "Cluster assignment check (2D)") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 2, alpha = 1))) +
  theme_bw()

title: 8 Peak Bead Tracking — Aurora EVO (5L)
text:
Per-peak metrics
The numbers actually tracked: for each detector × population, the median intensity, robust %CV (peak tightness), event count, and two QC flags. in_range is FALSE if the median sits at the detector ceiling; resolved is FALSE if the peak isn’t separated from its neighbour (e.g. dim peaks lost in a weak detector’s noise floor). Unresolved peaks still get a value but are excluded from trending. The example contrasts a strong detector (YG1-A, all 8 resolved) with a weak one (UV1-A, dim peaks merged).


Code
# For every detector x population: median intensity, robust %CV, event count,
# and two QC flags. "in_range" is FALSE when the median is at the detector
# ceiling (off-scale). "resolved" is FALSE when the peak is not separated from
# its neighbour (e.g. dim peaks merged into the noise floor of a weak detector);
# such peaks still get a median, but it should not be trended.
robust_cv <- function(x) 100 * (IQR(x) / 1.349) / abs(median(x))

peak_metrics <- function(ff, lab, name) {
  date <- parse_run_date(name)
  e    <- exprs(ff)
  rows <- lapply(detector_channels, function(d) {
    a   <- asinh(e[, d] / cluster_cofactor)            # for resolution only
    med_a <- tapply(a, lab, median)[as.character(1:n_peaks)]
    sd_a  <- tapply(a, lab, function(z) IQR(z) / 1.349)[as.character(1:n_peaks)]
    gap   <- pmin(c(Inf, diff(med_a)), c(diff(med_a), Inf))
    data.frame(
      file     = name,
      date     = date,
      detector = d,
      peak     = 1:n_peaks,
      median   = tapply(e[, d], lab, median)[as.character(1:n_peaks)],
      rcv      = tapply(e[, d], lab, robust_cv)[as.character(1:n_peaks)],
      n        = as.integer(table(factor(lab, levels = 1:n_peaks))),
      in_range = tapply(e[, d], lab, median)[as.character(1:n_peaks)] < biex_max,
      resolved = gap > resolution_k * sd_a
    )
  })
  bind_rows(rows)
}

8 Peak Bead Tracking — Aurora EVO (5L)
text:
Tracking over time
Each peak’s median intensity and %CV plotted against acquisition date, per detector, from the accumulated archive. Stable lines mean stable instrument performance; a step or drift flags a detector/laser problem. Only resolved, in-range peaks are shown. The two heatmaps give an executive overview before the detailed per-detector trends.

Per-laser overview
Collapses the 64 detectors into a 5-laser × dates heatmap of peak-8 deviation from baseline (first run for each detector, averaged across that laser’s detectors). A whole-row colour shift indicates a laser-level problem rather than a single detector. The first run is baseline so its row is 0% by construction.


Code
laser_of <- function(d) sub("[0-9]+-A$", "", as.character(d))

p8_base <- combined |>
  filter(peak == n_peaks, in_range) |>
  group_by(detector) |>
  slice_min(date, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  select(detector, base_median = median) |>
  ungroup()

laser_delta <- combined |>
  filter(peak == n_peaks, in_range) |>
  left_join(p8_base, by = "detector") |>
  mutate(delta_pct = (median - base_median) / base_median * 100,
         laser    = factor(laser_of(detector),
                           levels = c("UV", "V", "B", "YG", "R"))) |>
  group_by(laser, date) |>
  summarise(delta_pct = mean(delta_pct, na.rm = TRUE),
            n_det     = n(), .groups = "drop")

lim <- max(abs(laser_delta$delta_pct), na.rm = TRUE)
ggplot(laser_delta, aes(x = factor(date), y = laser, fill = delta_pct)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%+.1f%%", delta_pct)), size = 3) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#b2182b", mid = "white", high = "#2166ac",
                       midpoint = 0, limits = c(-lim, lim),
                       name = "Peak 8\nΔ vs t0") +
  labs(x = "Acquisition date", y = "Laser",
       title = "Per-laser peak-8 deviation from baseline",
       caption = "Cell = mean % change of peak 8 median from first run, across that laser's detectors (in-range only).") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10)











Resolution-count heatmap
For each detector × run, the number of peaks resolved (0–8). A row going darker over time is the cleanest signal of a detector losing its dim peaks — i.e. rising noise floor or falling gain.


Code
resolution <- combined |>
  group_by(date, detector) |>
  summarise(n_resolved = sum(resolved), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(resolution, aes(x = factor(date), y = detector, fill = n_resolved)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.1) +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = rev(detector_channels)) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "viridis", limits = c(0, n_peaks),
                       name = "Peaks\nresolved") +
  labs(x = "Acquisition date", y = NULL,
       title = "Peaks resolved per detector per run",
       caption = "0 = no peaks separated above noise; 8 = full RCP-30-5A staircase resolved.") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 9) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6))

# in-range peaks are plotted (unresolved peaks carry no trustworthy signal).
trend <- combined |>
  filter(resolved, in_range) |>
  mutate(peak = factor(peak, levels = 1:n_peaks))

ggplot(trend, aes(x = date, y = median, colour = peak, group = peak)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 1) +
  scale_y_flowjo_biexp(maxValue = biex_max, pos = biex_pos,

  facet_wrap(~ detector, scales = "free_y", ncol = 4) +
  labs(x = "Acquisition date", y = "Median intensity (biexponential scale)",
       colour = "Peak",
       title = "Per-peak median intensity over time",
       caption = "Resolved, in-range peaks only. Single run shown as points until more dates accumulate.") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 9) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 8),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 6, angle = 45, hjust = 1))

  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ detector, scales = "free_y", ncol = 4) +

       title = "Per-peak %CV over time",

  theme_bw(base_size = 9) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 8),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 6, angle = 45, hjust = 1))











Brightest peak (peak 8) %CV
The brightest population is normally the tightest (rCV ~1–2%), so any rise in its %CV is a sensitive indicator of detector linearity, saturation, or noise at the top of the dynamic range. One line per detector, in_range only.


Code

  filter(peak == n_peaks, in_range)

ggplot(peak8, aes(x = date, y = rcv, group = detector)) +
  geom_line(colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(size = 1.2, colour = "firebrick") +
  facet_wrap(~ detector, scales = "free_y", ncol = 4) +
  labs(x = "Acquisition date", y = "Peak 8 robust %CV",
       title = "Brightest peak (peak 8) %CV over time",
       caption = "In-range peak 8 only.") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 9) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 8),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 6, angle = 45, hjust = 1))











Blank peak (peak 1) %CV
The blank/dimmest population’s spread tracks the noise floor: a stable peak 1 %CV means consistent background; a rising one signals increased electronic noise, optical scatter contamination, or compensation issues. One line per detector, in_range only.

section: Staining index (peak 1 vs lowest resolved peak)
text:
Staining index (peak 1 vs lowest resolved peak)
How far the first resolved peak above the blank sits above peak 1, relative to peak 1’s own spread. Peak 1 is the “negative”; the positive is the lowest peak > 1 that is resolved and in range (surfaced as pos_peak so any change is visible).
\[\mathrm{SI} = \dfrac{\widetilde{m}_{\text{pos}} - \widetilde{m}_{1}}{2 \times \widetilde{\sigma}_{1}}\]
Medians (\(\widetilde{m}\)) and robust SD (\(\widetilde{\sigma} = \mathrm{IQR}/1.349\)) on raw intensity. A higher SI means cleaner separation of the dimmest detectable signal from background; a downward trend flags rising background or falling detector gain.


Code
si_per_detector <- function(g) {
  cand <- g$peak[g$peak > 1 & g$resolved & g$in_range]
  if (length(cand) == 0) {
    return(data.frame(pos_peak = NA_integer_,
                      median_pos = NA_real_,
                      median_1   = g$median[g$peak == 1],
                      rsd_1      = NA_real_, si = NA_real_))
  }
  p     <- min(cand)
  m1    <- g$median[g$peak == 1]
  rsd_1 <- abs(g$rcv[g$peak == 1] * m1 / 100)   # rSD recovered from rCV
  data.frame(pos_peak   = as.integer(p),
             median_pos = g$median[g$peak == p],
             median_1   = m1,
             rsd_1      = rsd_1,
             si         = (g$median[g$peak == p] - m1) / (2 * rsd_1))
}

si_summary <- combined |>
  group_by(file, date, detector) |>
  group_modify(~ si_per_detector(.x)) |>
  ungroup()

# Example: SI for a strong vs a weak detector across the available runs.
si_summary |>
  filter(detector %in% c("YG1-A", "B4-A", "V8-A", "UV1-A")) |>
  mutate(si = round(si, 2),
         median_pos = round(median_pos),
         median_1   = round(median_1),
         rsd_1      = round(rsd_1, 1)) |>
  arrange(detector, date)
